PRINCIPLE: Each test should focus on a single requirement/behavior (one Arrange-Act-Assert). RATIONALE: Single-focus tests make root cause identification precise. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if the test exercises exactly one act operation/behavior; non-compliant if it contains multiple distinct acts. DECISION RULES: The method calls getAntecessor before MST, callObterAgm to compute MST, then getAntecessor after MST — i.e., multiple distinct 'Act' operations (>1). The test name is generic and does not indicate a single scenario. VERDICT: non-compliant because the test mixes precondition behavior and post-MST behavior in the same method.

PRINCIPLE: Tests must not depend on other tests; use setup/teardown if needed. RATIONALE: Independence allows arbitrary execution order and parallel runs. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if tests use only local variables or use @Before/@After properly. DECISION RULES: The test uses only local variables (Grafo grafo0, AgmPrim agmPrim0) and does not reference or modify shared static/instance state in the visible method. No test ordering hints are present. VERDICT: compliant because the method uses only local state and shows no shared mutable state or ordering dependence.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Provide tests for both happy path and error scenarios for each method. RATIONALE: Ensures robustness and that exceptions are handled. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if there are at least two test methods covering happy and error cases (e.g., assertThrows). DECISION RULES: The class contains only this single test method; although it attempts to exercise a precondition (possible NPE) and a post-MST flow, the criterion requires at least two distinct tests per method under test. There is no separate test explicitly asserting an exception via assertThrows or a dedicated negative-case test. VERDICT: non-compliant because there's only one test method for the behavior and no distinct, explicit negative-case test.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should validate min/max/just-outside-boundary inputs. RATIONALE: Boundaries yield most off-by-one bugs. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if tests include empty, zero, negative, max, min or names indicating boundary tests. DECISION RULES: The test uses n=1069 and index 0; it does not exercise explicit boundary cases such as -1, n-1, Integer.MAX_VALUE, or empty graphs. Although it checks that antecessor is >= -1 and < n when non-null, it does not supply boundary inputs or explicit edge-case scenarios. VERDICT: non-compliant because explicit boundary inputs are not tested.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be self-contained and avoid duplication via helpers/constants. RATIONALE: Modularity reduces duplication and improves maintainability. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if helper methods or constants are used, or if tests are very short and non-repetitive. DECISION RULES: The method uses hard-coded magic value n=1069 and repeats setup calls inline. There are no private helper methods or constants defined in the visible code to improve reuse. VERDICT: non-compliant because setup is inlined with magic numbers and no helper/constant is present.
